Nothing.. and that's the problem. He doesn't do anything on his own except for watching tv, play video games, and mope around in his room. If I don't tell him to do it, he doesn't do it. He has no other hobbies, no other ambitions, it's really frustrating.

That's a good point. But, you don't just want to start taking stuff away without substituting something healthy.

It would be best to work on talking to him, and seeing where he's at. Not from a judgemental parental perspective either. Kids can react terribly to that. But, like peers. Find out what interests him, and work on replacing some of that game/tv time with it. Find something to do together. Sometimes, you can't get much out of them though and you just have to take the initiative and come up with something to try together. Something new.

He hasn't had video game privileges in months. TV is only when the family watches something together, maybe 3 hours a week. But he has unlimited book time or going outside time. He sometimes just lays in bed for hours doing nothing. Not even reading comic books.

I take it he is a preteen or a teen, right? I did a lot of game playing, and tv watching then too. But, I got out and ran around a lot. Before I could drive I was on my bicycle trying to flirt with teenagers, and when I could drive I was gone.

Have you tried casually chatting with him to see why he doesn't have a hobby, or what he may like to try?

I have, and it's just that he doesn't care about anything. In fact if I didn't force him to exercise, he would still be obese. When I realized how fat he was getting I put a stop to that right away. Maybe do some research in confidence building activities you guys can do together? A lot of my issues came from the way my parents were. And I'm not saying you're guilty of this, its just a story, so please don't read it that way. They meant well, but the way the pushed me forward was all wrong. It made me feel like I was always doing things wrong, and I couldn't get it right. But, dealing with kids, especially older ones, can be a shot in the dark sometimes. They're wired ass backwards.

Limited Resources 292 Magic Origins Set Review: Commons and Uncommons

My thoughts:

White is by far the best color in the format for drafting. It has great cards at all rarities, common, uncommon, and rare.

Red is a close second, with great commons and good uncommons, but a little less playable rares (which matters less in drafting, but matters a great deal in sealed).

Green has good commons and uncommons, nothing as strong but there are a few too many cute rares like Herald of the Pantheon and Evolutionary Leap. It also lacks decent removal.

Black is fourth, because while it has a decent amount of playable removal such as Reave Soul and such, the creatures are a little on the weak side. A lot of Black's creatures encourage loads and loads of trading, while not enough are able to close out the game. it has some great rares, though, like Korthophed, Languish, Priest of the Blood Rite, etc.

Blue is in last, because its commons are pretty weak except for one or two, and its great uncommons are few and far between. What it does have is lots and lots of tempo plays, like bouncing and counterspells. Being able to reset renown might make Blue a lot better than I thought, so I am open to being wrong.

It depends on what courier you use. If you use Fedex, or UPS then your package is guaranteed to get there, no problems (although you may have to pay some sort of import tax on it at collection time for certain reasons). If you use VN Postal system then your package will be pretty delayed, probably opened, 95% it gets to where it's going, ~ 5% of disappearing into the aether. Do not use DHL.

TL;DR: use Fedex. UPS is probably good too.
